newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: S&P revises Tenaga outlook to stable.
newsitem.headline: S&P revises Tenaga outlook to stable.

text.p: Standard and Poor's Corp said on Tuesday it had affirmed its A-plus rating on Tenaga Nasional Berhad and had revised its outlook to stable from positive.
The rating applies to both local and foreign currency obligations, the ratings agency said.

"The outlook revision reflects the continuing uncertainty of the regulatory and tariff regime in Malaysia, as well as the increasing financial pressures of Tenaga's ongoing large capital expenditure program," S&P said in a statement.
However, the government's commitment to its financial viability and its dominant position as an electricity supplier in Malaysia make Tenaga a strong company.
The government still holds 78 percent equity in the privatised utility.
Tenaga said last week it had forwarded a fresh tariff revision proposal to the government.
"The continuing uncertainty regarding electricity tariffs indicates the government's willingness to expose Tenaga to a greater degree of uncertainty and possible financial pressure," S&P said.

It said pressures on Tenaga include increased purchases from independent power producers (IPPs), high reserve margins, suspension of the tariff formula, and high levels of capital expenditure of around 33 billion ringgit up to the year 2001.
Tenaga generates 70 percent of Malaysia's power and IPPs around 30 percent. The state-run company retains its monopoly on power distribution.
